Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

C306 0.2.0

First release of the independently maintained version of C306 at https://github.com/TranHung93/306 (based on oucru-biostats/C306). Install it with remotes::install_github("TranHung93/306"); the package name is unchanged. Several bugs gave wrong numbers in tables or plots: check the section below before relying on reports made with earlier versions.

Impact on previous reports

Five bugs gave wrong numbers in tables or plots. Reports made in the periods below with the affected arguments should be re-run with this version. In each case, the other numbers in the same table were correct.

  1. Risk % in survival tables
    • Functions: sstable.survcomp(), sstable.survcomp.subgroup() (all rows), and tables built from them (ss_flextable(), ss_huxtable(), rbind()).
    • Affected: add.risk = TRUE (the default), with any compare.method. sstable.survcomp.subgroup() always uses it.
    • Period: 2024-07-09 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 40aeabd, “Adding mstate model to survcomp”; versions 0.1.5-022405 to 0.1.5-240715) until this version.
    • What was wrong: the “risk [%]” figure was 100 × the cumulative hazard, not the absolute risk (e.g. 232% instead of 92%). It is now 1 − Kaplan–Meier, or the Aalen–Johansen probability of the cause of interest for competing risks. Competing-risks tables were wrong from the start (same commit). Before 2024-07-09 the column was correct. Event counts, HRs, RMST/cumulative-incidence estimates, CIs and p-values were not affected.
  2. Subgroup rows with reference.arm = "A"
    • Function: sstable.survcomp.subgroup().
    • Affected: reference.arm = "A", subgroup rows only (not “All patients”).
    • Period: 2024-06-17 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit cbe10dc, when reference.arm was added) until this version.
    • What was wrong: subgroup rows ignored reference.arm and always used arm B as the reference, so their HR / RMST / cumulative-incidence comparisons were inverted relative to the “All patients” row (e.g. HR 0.54 shown instead of 1.85).
  3. model.censoring dropped from the heterogeneity test
    • Function: sstable.survcomp.subgroup().
    • Affected: compare.method = "rmst" or "cuminc" with model.censoring given in compare.args; the “Test for heterogeneity” p-value only.
    • Period: 2024-06-13 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 869429c, “add RMST to survcomp”) until this version.
    • What was wrong: the user’s model.censoring was replaced by the eventglm default ("independent") in the interaction test, so the heterogeneity p-value used a different censoring model from the one requested (e.g. 0.795 instead of 0.375).
  4. Confidence intervals of subgroup_effect()
    • Function: subgroup_effect(), including sstable = TRUE, flextable = TRUE and transpose = TRUE output.
    • Affected: all calls, both method = "lik.ratio" and "wald"; the CI.lower / CI.upper columns only.
    • Period: 2019-12-26 (upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 5b44416, when the function was added) until this version.
    • What was wrong: the CI was that of the log odds ratio, printed next to the odds ratio (e.g. OR 1.06 with “CI” (-0.20, 0.32) instead of (0.82, 1.37)). It is now the CI of the OR, as in logist_summary(). ORs, log ORs and p-values were correct.
  5. Drift of the competing-risks curves
    • Functions: gg_ajsurvplot() (from 2024-06-20, upstream oucru-biostats/C306 commit 17a757d) and gg_ajsurvplot2(), including .return_data = TRUE (from 2024-06-25, upstream commit b89f64b), until this version.
    • Affected: plots with groups on the right-hand side of the formula whose censoring patterns differ.
    • What was wrong: the censoring weights were pooled over all groups, so the curves were not the Aalen–Johansen estimate of each group. They drifted in late follow-up (by up to 2.5 percentage points in survival::mgus2 by sex). Early follow-up was essentially unchanged. The curves are now exact Aalen–Johansen estimates. Fine–Gray hazard ratios in sstable.survcomp() were not affected (they correctly use pooled weights).

Other changes to output

  • sstable.survcomp.subgroup(): the “All patients” row now uses pdigits (it was fixed at 3; only the number of digits shown changes).
  • sstable.baseline(): when the column variable is a character vector, its columns are now in reverse alphabetical order (e.g. B then A), the same as for factor arms and as in sstable.ae(). Previously character arms were in alphabetical order.
  • sstable.ae(): grade rows are in clinical order (Grade 1, 2, … 10, or I, II, … V; a factor keeps its level order), with “Grade N/A” last. Before, they were in alphabetical order (“Grade 10” before “Grade 2”, “Grade N/A” first).
  • logist_summary(method = "lik.ratio"): rows are in model term order, as with method = "wald" (they were sorted alphabetically).
  • logist_summary() for a model without intercept: the footer said that likelihood ratio p-values were not calculated, but they are (and are valid). It now says what they test.
  • myformat.data(): factor codes that are not in the dictionary are kept as extra levels, with a warning, instead of becoming NA. inspect.data() then reports them as “Out of range” instead of “Missing value”.
  • pct(method = "cont") with exactly two ranges returns the percentage of each range (before: a single number, the second range only).
  • contSummary() replaces only whole statistic names (any case) and keeps the rest of your text as written. Before, it lower-cased the whole string (“IQR” became “iqr”) and replaced names inside words (“minimum” became “1.0imum”). Output for the default statistics is unchanged. Statistics of all-missing data are NA without warnings (before: NaN, Inf and a warning).

Bug fixes

  • sstable.baseline() no longer fails with “replacement has length zero” when the formula has a single row variable (e.g. x ~ arm).
  • sstable.baseline() no longer creates a copy of each summarised variable in the global environment.
  • sstable.ae() with flextable = TRUE no longer fails with “could not find function as_paragraph” when flextable is not attached.
  • sstable.ae() no longer changes options(warn), and reports adverse events classified into more than one group with a single warning instead of printing to the console.
  • sstable.ae(): the flextable footer now describes the test actually used. It has no p-value note when test = FALSE, and says “Fisher’s exact test” when chisq.test = FALSE. User footers are no longer merged into the wrong footer row.
  • sstable.ae() with a factor grade.var containing NA shows the missing grades as “Grade N/A” (they were dropped with a warning).
  • simple_recode(): numeric input stays numeric (it was returned as character). A factor stays a factor with recoded levels; previously a 2-level factor came back as all NA and other factors as character. A 2-level factor recoded to "TRUE"/"FALSE" still becomes logical.
  • pct() with method = "fct" no longer returns NA for every level when the data contain missing values, and works on character vectors.
  • labAE() works again with dplyr >= 1.1.0 (it always failed with “... must be empty”).
  • getlabel() on a data frame with meta no longer fails, and returns labels in the column order of the data.
  • ss_flextable() now uses its bg argument (it was ignored).
  • ss_huxtable() accepts the objects returned by sstable.baseline(), sstable.ae() and sstable.survcomp() (it failed with “sstable must be a matrix or data frame”; only ss_flextable() had a method for them).
  • ss_header(), ss_body() and ss_section() now return an ss_tbl object.
  • rbind.ss_obj() called directly no longer fails.
  • sstable.survcomp() no longer fails when only one arm is present in the data with medsum = TRUE. The missing arm is shown as “-”.
  • sstable.survcomp.subgroup() no longer fails when a subgroup variable has an empty level; that row is shown as “-”.
  • logist_summary(flextable = TRUE) and subgroup_effect(flextable = TRUE) work. They always failed with “invalid row selection”, because ss_flextable() failed on tables with a single header row.
  • logist_summary() works for models with a single coefficient.
  • ss_flextable() merges and bolds the right row for section rows (it used the row number of the whole table, including headers, as the body row number).
  • as_sstable() on a list with a list body works (it always failed with “the condition has length > 1”).
  • ss_format(.guess = FALSE) gives its intended message when rows are not classified, instead of “invalid ‘type’ (list) of argument”.
  • inspect.data() works without an explicit check_missing (it always failed with “the condition has length > 1” on R >= 4.2). It reports “No error was found!” with message().
  • convert.info() works in UTF-8 locales (the default on Windows since R 4.2, and on Linux/macOS). It always failed with “‘pattern’ is invalid”. Category labels are now transliterated to ASCII (e.g. “Nữ” becomes “Nu”) instead of losing their non-ASCII letters.
  • import.info() works when the dictionary has grids but none is requested.
  • gg_ajsurvplot() and gg_ajsurvplot2() work when data is not a global variable (e.g. inside a function); they failed with “object not found”.
  • mutate_f() on an ungrouped data frame keeps the name of a single new column.
  • createProject() now creates the RStudio project file (<dir>.Rproj) when the package is installed normally. The template .Rproj was left out of the built package by .Rbuildignore, so it was only created when the package was loaded from source.
  • sstable.baseline(), sstable.ae(), sstable.survcomp() and sstable.survcomp.subgroup() with flextable = TRUE no longer fail when a group or arm name contains an apostrophe or a backslash (e.g. “O’Brien”). They failed with “unexpected symbol” or “unrecognized escape”, because the header labels were pasted into R code and run with eval(parse()). (A backslash that forms a valid escape, such as a literal \t, did not fail but was shown as a tab.) Output for other names is unchanged.

Input checking

  • The main functions now check their inputs and stop with a clear message (condition class c306_input_error) instead of a cryptic error, a warning, or wrong output. This covers sstable.baseline(), sstable.ae(), sstable.survcomp(), sstable.survcomp.subgroup(), logist_summary(), subgroup_effect(), pct(), simple_recode(), contSummary(), labAE() and createProject(). The checks include:
    • data frames, and data with zero rows;
    • variables missing from the data, with their names listed;
    • the formula shape (e.g. a survival model must have Surv() on the left);
    • TRUE/FALSE arguments, digits, pcutoff, and time > 0. Inputs that were silently accepted and gave wrong results now give an error: pdigits = -1, time = -1, an empty fullid_data, and character grades in labAE().
  • Variables used in sstable.baseline() formulas must be columns of data. (Variables from the calling environment never worked.)
  • createProject() now stops with an error for an unknown structure or a non-empty dir. Before, it reported success even when nothing was copied. It reports with message() instead of printing, and returns the project path invisibly.
  • ss_huxtable(), ht_theme_markdown() and ht_theme_kable() now say clearly when the suggested package huxtable is not installed.

Changes to function signatures

The following S3 methods now have the same arguments as their generics (as required by R CMD check). Calls with positional arguments work as before.

  • explicit.lm(x, ...): explicit.lm(fit = ) is deprecated.
  • simple_relevel.data.frame(x, ..., by): simple_relevel.data.frame(data = ) is deprecated. simple_relevel.default() gains ....
  • print.ss_tbl(x, pretty, ...): print.ss_tbl(sstable = ) is deprecated.
  • rbind.ss_ae(), rbind.ss_baseline(), rbind.ss_survcomp(), rbind.ss_obj() now take the tables through .... rbind(tbl1, tbl2), positional header/footer, and tbl1 =/tbl2 = all keep working.

Performance

  • inspect.data() is about 7 times faster on large data (e.g. 5.8 s to 0.8 s for 20,000 rows × 60 numeric variables). Numeric variables are no longer converted to text to look for empty strings, and each variable’s errors are collected before one data frame is built. The output is unchanged.

Package infrastructure

  • This version is maintained independently at https://github.com/TranHung93/306 (based on oucru-biostats/C306); install it with remotes::install_github("TranHung93/306"). The package name stays C306.
  • The bundled example datasets are now simulated. inst/extdata/baseline_data.csv and inst/extdata/ae_data.csv used to contain real trial data. They have been replaced by synthetic data with the same columns, types, factor levels and a similar pattern of missing values (IDs SIM-001 etc.), generated reproducibly by data-raw/simulate_data.R. The same data are now also available as documented datasets (baseline_data, ae_data). Examples, the vignette and the README therefore show different numbers from earlier versions. The real data have been removed from the repository history, so commit hashes differ from those in oucru-biostats/C306; the commits cited above are labelled as upstream commits.
  • Added a LICENSE file, a testthat (3rd edition) test suite, and this NEWS file.
  • crayon, assertthat and stringr are no longer used. Hmisc moved from Imports to Suggests (it is only used in a vignette). lifecycle and the base packages stats, utils, graphics, grDevices and methods were added to Imports. MASS was added to Suggests (tests only). ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 is required.
  • Vignettes now build as HTML vignettes and no longer write files into the working directory.
